declared_purpose: Automatic, structured, persistent agent memory with importance scoring, decay, reinforcement and retrieval; supported domains include user facts, agent identity, relationships and world knowledge. A unified brain dashboard is also declared. These outcomes are explicit; transcript breadth, staging lifetime, full-index backups and external font loading are implementation choices (SKILL.md:4-24,58-107).

data_operations.operation: Initialize local storage and optionally register scheduled agent tasks
data_operations.data_scope: Empty memory index, domain directories, signal-limit preference and static task instructions containing workspace paths
data_operations.condition: Installation creates the index only if absent. --with-cron registers tasks when openclaw is available; otherwise it prints commands. Registration does not itself send conversation content.

data_operations.data_scope: All session files for AGENT_ID, default main; JSON records are read before selecting user and assistant messages newer than a usable timestamp watermark
data_operations.condition: Runs directly or through the encoding pipeline. --full ignores the watermark; absent, invalid or legacy message-ID watermarks start fresh. This is a local read, not demonstrated remote disclosure.

data_operations.source: Selected user and assistant message text
data_operations.data_scope: First text block or string, truncated to 500 characters before cleanup; retained message ID, timestamp, role and cleaned text. Filters remove specified markup, CJK text and several noise patterns; they do not implement credential-field redaction.
data_operations.condition: Qualifying messages are sorted across sessions. An explicitly supplied --limit caps the output after collection; the output file is overwritten.

data_operations.operation: Infer importance and categories; reinforce existing memories and stage new candidates
data_operations.data_scope: Heuristic emotional, preference, decision, relationship, project and identity labels; text similarity; importance, access dates and reinforcement counts; pending raw text, role, reason, domain, category and date
data_operations.condition: Scores below 0.5 are skipped. Word-set similarity above 0.6 reinforces an existing memory by 10% of remaining headroom; other qualifying signals become pending candidates. The 800-character pending cap cannot restore text removed by preprocessing. Labels are inferred, not verified attributes.

data_operations.operation: Return batches to the summarization caller and instruct memory creation
data_operations.data_scope: Default batch of 30 filtered candidates; up to 300 characters of each candidate plus importance and file paths in stdout; requested summaries of at most 80 characters with memory metadata
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Invoking caller or sub-agent context; remaining candidates persist in pending-memories.json
data_operations.condition: summarize-pending.sh must be invoked separately. It prints instructions rather than calling an LLM or writing summaries itself. It removes the current batch from pending storage when more remain; final-file deletion and index updates require the caller to follow its instructions. A normal tool return can remain with that caller.

data_operations.data_scope: Pending candidates, requested summaries of approximately 100 characters and updates to the memory index
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: OpenClaw isolated cron agent context; index.json and HIPPOCAMPUS_CORE.md
data_operations.condition: --with-cron installs instructions to run the pipeline with --no-spawn, inspect pending content using head -20, summarize, update the index, delete pending storage and sync core memories. Agent compliance, model routing and remote processing are unresolved. The standalone pipeline only prints a spawn command; it does not execute it.

data_operations.source: Recent main-session history, preprocessed signals, or current-session context, depending on the selected instructions
data_operations.data_scope: History path requests 20 messages with includeTools:false; agentdir path reads signals.jsonl and the complete index. Instructions select user, self, relationship and world memories, reinforce matches and persist index updates.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Applicable background/main agent context and memory/index.json
data_operations.condition: These are distinct instructed paths, not proof that all run together. Optional configuration names Anthropic models, but supplied source does not establish a remote endpoint, actual model invocation or provider retention.

data_operations.operation: Back up the full index, decay scores and flag archival candidates
data_operations.data_scope: Backup includes every memory and its metadata. Decay changes importance and run/update timestamps; stdout reports IDs and scores.
data_operations.condition: Backup occurs before the same-day skip check and overwrites the previous backup. Eligible memories lose importance; low scores produce review suggestions. This script neither archives nor deletes memory content.

data_operations.operation: Return selected memories for session context or query recall
data_operations.source: memory/index.json and, for recall, the caller's query
data_operations.data_scope: load-core returns memory contents above THRESHOLD, default 0.7. recall returns keyword-matching contents, IDs, domains, categories and scores, default top five with minimum combined score 0.3.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Invoking caller through stdout; intended session context when integrated
data_operations.condition: Scripts run when invoked. Both read the local index; neither script writes access-date updates. Their returns do not independently establish disclosure to another recipient.

data_operations.operation: Persist a derived core-memory document for context and RAG
data_operations.data_scope: Contents and importance scores of memories above THRESHOLD, default 0.75, grouped by domain with generation metadata
data_operations.condition: sync-core.sh overwrites the markdown file. OpenClaw indexing depends on the separately recommended memorySearch.extraPaths configuration; its backend, embeddings and retention are not supplied.

data_operations.operation: Read identity and other brain-state files; persist a dashboard snapshot
data_operations.source: IDENTITY.md, configured or fallback avatar file, memory/index.json, emotional-state.json and optional reward-state.json
data_operations.data_scope: Agent name and full avatar bytes; memory counts and five highest-importance memory excerpts; emotional dimensions and five recent emotion labels, intensities and triggers; optional drive, seeking, anticipating and five recent reward records. Mood labels are derived from emotional dimensions.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Local generator and $WORKSPACE/brain-dashboard.html, including embedded avatar and inline state data
data_operations.condition: Generation requires an index. Amygdala reads are unconditional despite optional-skill documentation; missing or invalid emotional-state data can terminate execution under set -e before HTML is written. VTA reads are conditional. Persistence requires successful generation.

data_operations.source: Generated dashboard CSS and rendered README badge images
data_operations.data_scope: Requests for the Inter stylesheet or static badge images; network request metadata, with exact headers and referrer behavior unresolved. No memory payload is explicitly placed in these URLs.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: fonts.googleapis.com for the dashboard stylesheet; img.shields.io for README badges
data_operations.condition: A browser or Markdown renderer must load the respective external resources. Dashboard generation alone does not fetch the stylesheet. Further resources referenced by the external stylesheet are unknown.

data_operations.operation: Guide consolidation, relationship inference and reflection persistence
data_operations.source: Recent daily notes, conversation experiences and reflection prompts
data_operations.data_scope: Preferences, job/location/project context, behavioral patterns, inferred trust and relationship changes, and agent identity or opinions
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Domain memory files, MEMORY.md, daily notes and self-reflection files
data_operations.condition: Agent-followed guidance, not automatic writes by the helper scripts. Consolidation permits deletion of routine logs after a month and archival/removal of dated context; this is discretionary guidance, not an enforced retention policy.

data_operations.operation: Guide contextual and proactive memory searches
data_operations.source: Current topics and stored memory documents
data_operations.data_scope: Queries about decisions, preferences, relationships, agent development and projects; related domain files, MEMORY.md and daily notes
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: memory_search tool and requesting agent; external search/index infrastructure unresolved
data_operations.condition: The agent must follow the recall guidance. It includes proactive searches when starting projects or encountering familiar or emotional topics. Tool returns may remain with the requesting agent.

potential_excess.data_scope: Qualifying historical signals beyond the promised first-run limit, including cleaned text, roles, IDs and timestamps
potential_excess.condition: Normal pipeline execution without a usable watermark. Installation saves a default limit of 100 or a custom limit, but the pipeline supplies no --limit and preprocessing does not read .signal-limit.
potential_excess.purpose_basis: The entry explicitly promises a bounded initial encoding by default; whole-history processing is a separate option.
potential_excess.necessary_behavior: Find recent qualifying signals across sessions and encode the selected initial window. Reading older files locally may still be needed to identify that window.
potential_excess.proposed_reduction: Consume the saved first-run preference and apply the selected limit before writing signals and scoring them. Preserve explicit whole-history and direct --full behavior.
potential_excess.preservation_conditions: Keep chronological cross-session selection, usable-watermark incremental processing and explicitly requested history breadth.

potential_excess.data_scope: Raw cleaned signal text and message metadata after downstream processing has consumed or staged it
potential_excess.condition: Preprocessing writes the file; encoding and summarization contain no signal-file cleanup. It remains until overwritten or removed outside the supplied flow, including pipeline early-return paths.
potential_excess.purpose_basis: The entry labels signals.jsonl temporary. Persistent concise memories are the intended durable outcome.
potential_excess.necessary_behavior: Retain signals while scoring and safely staging pending candidates; preserve enough state to recover from processing failures.
potential_excess.proposed_reduction: Delete the signal staging file after successful durable staging/index updates, with explicit cleanup on successful empty runs. Keep pending candidates until summarization succeeds.
potential_excess.preservation_conditions: Do not remove the only recoverable copy before downstream writes succeed. This narrows duplicate staging lifetime, not required pending data or final memories.

potential_excess.data_scope: Complete memory index copied during an already-completed daily decay run
potential_excess.condition: Every invocation copies the index before testing whether decay already ran that day.
potential_excess.purpose_basis: Daily decay requires no index modification when the same-day guard skips work.
potential_excess.necessary_behavior: Check decayLastRun and return on a same-day repeat.
potential_excess.proposed_reduction: Move the same-day guard before backup creation. This removes a redundant persistence action.
potential_excess.preservation_conditions: Keep rollback protection for invocations that actually modify decay state.

potential_excess.data_scope: Memory contents, keywords and other unchanged personal fields in the decay backup
potential_excess.condition: An invocation proceeds with decay; the backup contains the entire index although decay changes only scores and run/update metadata.
potential_excess.purpose_basis: The backup supports recovery from score modification; a full content snapshot is an implementation choice.
potential_excess.necessary_behavior: Recover pre-decay importance values and metadata if an update fails.
potential_excess.proposed_reduction: Back up only affected IDs, scores and changed metadata, or use a transient full backup with cleanup after verified success. This narrows data in a recovery action rather than eliminating recovery.
potential_excess.preservation_conditions: Ensure reliable rollback and atomic writes; retain broader snapshots only for a separately established recovery requirement.

potential_excess.data_scope: Top-memory IDs and domains, recent-emotion intensities and recent-reward intensities
potential_excess.condition: Successful dashboard generation embeds these fields, but the supplied rendering code uses importance/summary, emotion label/trigger and reward type/source respectively.
potential_excess.purpose_basis: The dashboard requires the displayed values; these additional fields do not support its current rendering.
potential_excess.necessary_behavior: Persist the values needed to render the declared memory, emotion and drive views.
potential_excess.proposed_reduction: Omit unused fields from the generated snapshot. This reduces extra data within a required dashboard-generation action.
potential_excess.preservation_conditions: Preserve displayed summaries, scores, emotion descriptions, reward descriptions and tab behavior.

potential_excess.data_scope: Browser network metadata associated with loading a presentation font
potential_excess.recipient_or_storage: fonts.googleapis.com; any downstream stylesheet-selected resource recipients are unresolved
potential_excess.condition: A browser opens the generated dashboard and permits the CSS import.
potential_excess.purpose_basis: The declared dashboard presents local memory and brain-state information; retrieving a remote font is optional styling.
potential_excess.necessary_behavior: Render the dashboard with a readable font.
potential_excess.proposed_reduction: Remove the external import and use the existing system-font fallbacks or a packaged font. This removes a presentation-only remote request.
potential_excess.preservation_conditions: Preserve dashboard content, readability and interactions; exact Inter typography need not be preserved.

unknowns: All supplied files were reviewed. End-to-end model disclosure, OpenClaw RAG persistence and actual agent-performed updates/deletions remain unresolved because host implementations, runtime configuration and execution records are absent; these limits make the audit partial.

Optional configurations name Anthropic models, but actual provider endpoints, transmitted context, logging, retention and deletion behavior are undocumented. A tool return or configured model name alone does not establish a separate remote disclosure.

The pipeline does not execute its advertised spawn step, and summarize-pending.sh emits agent instructions. Whether cron or another caller completes summarization, semantic deduplication, index writes and pending-file deletion cannot be established.

OpenClaw memory_search query handling, embedding providers, additional indexes, context injection and deletion propagation are unavailable. Removing an index entry would not demonstrate removal from backups, core markdown, dashboards or external indexes.

No runtime data is supplied, so actual credentials, sensitive facts and generated inferences cannot be identified. Source filters truncate and remove selected patterns without a demonstrated sensitive-field redaction policy.

Browser headers, referrers, caching and downstream font-resource requests are unknown. Dashboard values are inserted into inline script and innerHTML without demonstrated escaping; content-dependent browser behavior cannot be bounded from the supplied runtime-free evidence.
Low importance only triggers archival review. No packaged automatic expiry or coordinated deletion mechanism establishes how long final memories and their derived copies remain.
